## Objective
- Build a complete, playable bilingual French/English AI chat and character-creation experience from the user's concept.

## Requirements
- Support French and English chat with AI characters and user-created characters.
- Keep characters private and allow saving with an address and password.
- Disallow nudity and sexual content in images/videos; swimsuits, dresses, and sexy styles are allowed.
- Include a detailed tutorial.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them upon completion.

## Decisions
- Implemented a static HTML/CSS/JavaScript experience with a local, rule-based chat engine and browser-based persistence.
- Account backup uses local encrypted storage; no server or cross-device sync is implemented.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the bilingual interface, chat, character library and creator, privacy/content guidelines, tutorial, and encrypted local backup flow.
- Added responsive styling and downloaded font assets.
- `node --check js/app.js` completed without errors.

### Active
- Verify the app in a browser, exercise its main flows, and capture/read a current small JPEG screenshot.

1. Run the app and check chat, language toggle, character creation/edit/delete, tutorial, safety rules, and encrypted backup.
2. Save and inspect a current JPEG screenshot at a viewport no wider than 1280px.
3. Fix any issues found and summarize the implementation and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: static application entry point.
- `css/style.css`: interface styling and responsive layouts.
- `js/app.js`: application behavior, bilingual content, local chat, privacy and backup logic.
- `assets/fonts/`: Manrope and Instrument Serif font files.
- `start.sh`: project startup script.
- `capture.sh`: capture script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed new files including `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, scripts, assets, and app files.
- The chat engine is local and template-based, not connected to an external AI service.
- Encrypted backups are stored in the same browser’s local storage; the interface can download the encrypted backup.
